title: . . . and the Special Circumstances When They Do
coreMove: Rewards work best after fair pay is settled, the task is routine, and people receive rationale, respect, and some choice.

exampleSpecs.audience: Farah, an operations lead choosing a modest routine-task reward
exampleSpecs.stakes: A warehouse checklist is late because the work is dull and easy to postpone.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show a reward that fits because the task is routine and bounded.

exampleSpecs.audience: Luis, a records supervisor explaining necessary dull work
exampleSpecs.stakes: A hospital cleanup has to happen, but staff resent the extra paperwork.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Pair a dull task with rationale and some choice.

exampleSpecs.audience: Anwen, a tax office manager repairing baseline fairness first
exampleSpecs.stakes: A backlog bonus is being proposed while temporary staff are underpaid.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Show fair compensation preceding incentive design.

exampleSpecs.audience: Gideon, a librarian acknowledging routine work without insulting it
exampleSpecs.stakes: A shelving project needs speed and accuracy but offers little variety.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use acknowledgment and method choice with a routine task.

exampleSpecs.audience: Rina, a field-service manager keeping incentives out of judgment work
exampleSpecs.stakes: A maintenance route includes both routine checks and customer diagnosis.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Separate algorithmic tasks from judgment tasks.

exampleSpecs.audience: Sol, a data migration lead choosing appreciation after the fact
exampleSpecs.stakes: A migration needs accuracy more than a race for prizes.
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Use a now-that reward as thanks, not a lever.
